*Upādinnattika* is a canonical Abhidhamma text located within the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Designated as section 13.4 in modern cataloging schemes, the text examines conditional relations in the context of the triad (*tika*) concerning phenomena that are clung to or grasped (*upādinna*) [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported in SuttaCentral or matched with significant scores in DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, however, DharmaNexus records widespread formulaic text reuse reflecting the highly standardized relational phrasing of the *Paṭṭhāna*, identifying 1,141 matching passages across 103 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest degree of textual overlap occurs with other expositions of the same triad or related structural combinations in the collection, foremost among them the *Upādinnattika* of Patthana 1.5 (290 matches; including segment alignment §8.1–11.1 with §260.1_2–270.1_0), as well as *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10), *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1), and *Upādinnattika* (Patthana 19.4) [DharmaNexus].
